walkthroughs.body_html:
A tropical storm is a giant low-pressure system with:

• Winds over 119 km/h
• Torrential rain
• Storm surges
• A spinning structure

Same storm — different names by region!

The same type of storm has different names:

• Hurricane — Atlantic / NE Pacific
• Typhoon — NW Pacific (Japan, Philippines)
• Cyclone — Indian Ocean, Australia

Wind speed and structure are identical.

Tropical storms have three key parts:

1. Eye — calm, clear centre (~30 km wide)
2. Eyewall — strongest winds, heaviest rain
3. Rain bands — spiral arms of cloud

The eyewall is the most dangerous part.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.

sequence.def: Warm sea supplies energy and moisture
Moist air rises, creating intense low pressure
Clouds form; released heat powers the storm
Coriolis effect spins the system; winds strengthen
Calm centre ringed by the eyewall's strongest winds
Cut off from warm water, the storm weakens
